destination.title: Dark-energy cosmology: mechanisms, inference, interactions and cosmic futures
destination.question: How can dark-energy behavior and its relation to matter be modeled and tested through cosmic expansion, perturbations, microscopic consistency and future evolution?
destination.summary: No original verbal region definition was supplied; this critique concerns numerical membership. The cohort mixes physical questions, settings, methods, conditional claims and adjacent dark-matter topics. The proposed family preserves those distinctions and routes sources outside its acceleration-centered scope to alternate homes.

systems: Scalar, fluid, thermal and interacting dark sectors
Modified-gravity and geometric effective dark sectors
targets: Origins and histories of cosmic acceleration
Coincidence, future evolution and conditional consistency tests
regimes: Earlier epochs and future evolution when explicitly connected to the source question
assumptions: Model assumptions remain local to each source.
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work remains eligible.
Conjectures are conditional hypotheses, not established selection rules.
conventions: Canonical scalar, effective fluid and total-energy scalar representations remain distinct.
Effective-density sign, effective phantom behavior and scalar kinetic sign are separate properties.
Background agreement does not establish perturbative or future equivalence.
includes: Mechanism, inference, method and consistency questions with explicit contribution roles
Unconstructed research directions and historical comparisons with visible status
excludes: Treating every numerical member as the same scoped question
Treating dark-matter production or detection alone as evidence about late acceleration
Universal observational or quantum-gravity conclusions from bounded excerpts

sources.title: Possible Theoretical limits on holographic quintessence from weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: The background specifies how the matter fraction and holographic dark energy determine cosmic expansion before converting the dark-energy fluid into a scalar trajectory.

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: The scalar excursion depends on how the dark component shares the expansion rate with independently specified matter. Distinguishing baryon-only matter from a separate dark-matter component is essential when a Chaplygin fluid may itself unify dark matter and dark energy.

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Can tachyon or generalized Born–Infeld descriptions evade the difficulty found for canonical Chaplygin reconstructions? The paper explicitly leaves this question open and supplies no corresponding quantum-gravity bound or noncanonical calculation.

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a canonical scalar describe the specified dark-energy histories while traversing less than one reduced Planck mass? For constant w, the analysis retains the degeneracy between equation of state and present matter abundance and compares it with cosmological observations.

sources.title: Dark Energy: A Brief Review

evidence.text: What could explain a small, nonzero dark-energy density and its present comparability to matter, and how can expansion and structure-growth observations distinguish proposed explanations?

sources.title: The Effective Field Theory of Dark Energy

evidence.text: Can single-field dark energy and modified gravity be organized into one action for cosmological perturbations, separating background evolution from clustering effects and systematically diagnosing scalar–gravity mixing and stability?

sources.title: Cosmological Evolution With Interaction Between Dark Energy And Dark Matter

evidence.text: How can energy exchange between dark energy and dark matter change cosmological evolution, including density scaling, accelerated expansion, the coincidence problem and structure formation? This is a review of multiple interaction models.

sources.title: Dark D-brane Cosmology

evidence.text: Can a moving hidden-sector D-brane supply interacting dark matter and DBI dark energy with geometrically determined couplings, accelerating scaling evolution, and a possible explanation for a small dynamical dark-energy density?

sources.title: Disformal couplings and the dark sector of the universe

evidence.text: Can background cosmology, CMB anisotropies, and linear structure growth distinguish conformal from disformal dark-sector couplings? The paper also asks whether a disformal term can suppress otherwise large conformal interactions and whether negative disformal factors cause instabilities.

sources.title: Dynamical systems applied to cosmology: dark energy and modified gravity

evidence.text: How can autonomous dynamical systems characterize cosmological evolution, especially late-time acceleration, and identify dark-energy models with suitable asymptotic behavior?

sources.title: Building Supergravity Quintessence Model

evidence.text: The model-building target is dynamical dark energy in supergravity. A viable scalar must avoid a gravitino-scale mass, retain sufficiently slow evolution at the present Hubble scale, and couple weakly enough to ordinary matter to pass gravitational tests.

sources.title: Unraveling the effective fluid approach for $f(R)$ models in the subhorizon approximation

evidence.text: Can viable metric f(R) models be described by an explicit effective dark-energy fluid under a controlled subhorizon approximation, with useful initial conditions, Boltzmann-code predictions and cosmological constraints?

sources.title: Emergent Dark Universe and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: The hEDU setting attributes the dark sector to extrinsic geometry rather than additional matter on the hypersurface. Ordinary matter sources a four-dimensional induced-gravity equation supplemented by a Brown–York boundary stress tensor.

sources.title: Designing Horndeski and the effective fluid approach

evidence.text: Can the gravitational-wave-compatible Horndeski subclass be represented by a tractable effective dark-energy fluid, and can designer models reproduce the ΛCDM background while retaining distinguishable, controlled perturbations?

sources.title: Dark Energy, the Swampland and the Equivalence Principle

evidence.text: How does a dark-matter-only scalar coupling alter late expansion and clustering while ordinary matter retains its usual metric? The initial EFT contains canonical quintessence, an exponential potential, and one nonrelativistic dark-matter species.

sources.title: $H_0$ tension, swampland conjectures, and the epoch of fading dark matter

evidence.text: The potential arranges a subdominant early scalar and a recent dark-energy-dominated universe. Its crossover is placed at the same field value as the onset of dark-matter fading, providing one shared threshold for two phenomenological changes.

sources.title: Forays into the dark side of the swamp

evidence.text: Can a homogeneous rolling dark-energy field induce particle-parameter changes relevant to dark-matter structure, freeze-in production, and electroweak stability?

sources.title: The Coincidence Problem and the Swampland Conjectures in the Ijjas-Steinhardt Cyclic Model of the Universe

evidence.text: Earlier models replace an indefinitely long dark-energy future with a finite lifetime or repeated cycles, allowing a comparable-density interval to occupy a nonvanishing fraction of cosmic time.

sources.title: Interplay between Swampland and Bayesian Machine Learning in constraining cosmological models

evidence.text: Which conclusions survive changes in expansion ansatz, generative probability model and matter–dark-energy interpretation, and can explicit valid scalar histories exhibit changes in the selected Swampland diagnostic classification?

sources.title: Consistency of Cubic Galileon Cosmology: Model-Independent Bounds from Background Expansion and Perturbative Analyses

evidence.text: Can a stable dark-energy model permit phantom behavior, improve the conditional reconstructed growth comparison and avoid an unwanted future de Sitter attractor? The paper nominates this combination as a research direction without constructing a solution.

sources.title: Swampland Conjectures and Cosmological Expansion

evidence.text: Can a finite scalar-field excursion compatible with the adopted swampland conjectures last through the expansion needed for entropy disposal in CBE cyclic cosmology? The proposed comparison concerns future evolution constrained indirectly by present dark-energy behavior.

sources.title: The effective fluid approach for modified gravity

evidence.text: How can modified gravity be represented as an effective dark-energy fluid and implemented simply in an Einstein–Boltzmann solver, including models whose background expansion is degenerate with ΛCDM?

sources.title: On finite time singularities in scalar field dark energy models based in the RS-II Braneworld

evidence.text: Can scalar dark energy on an RS-II brane develop finite-time cosmological singularities, and do initial conditions or the de Sitter Swampland bound change their occurrence? The paper compares dynamical-variable blowups with a separate classification based on an assumed Hubble history.

sources.title: Cosmological implications of an interacting model of dark matter & dark energy

evidence.text: How does a phenomenological dark matter–dark energy interaction, combined with a prescribed expansion history, affect cosmological evolution, energy conditions, stability diagnostics, and scalar-field swampland tests?

sources.title: Unexplored regions in teleparallel <math display="inline"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> gravity: Sign-changing dark energy density

evidence.text: Does relaxing positivity of effective dark-energy density reveal overlooked solutions of exponential infrared f(T) gravity, particularly negative-to-positive density transitions and expansion histories relevant to cosmological tensions?

sources.title: A Dynamical solution to the problem of a small cosmological constant and late time cosmic acceleration

evidence.text: Can nonlinear kinetic scalar dynamics explain why negative-pressure dark energy becomes important only recently, by linking its evolution to matter–radiation equality rather than tuning an initially tiny dark-energy density?

sources.title: Hybrid dark sector: Locked quintessence and dark matter

evidence.text: Can coupled supersymmetric flat-direction scalars account for dark matter and present dark energy, attain suitable initial conditions after inflation, and terminate accelerated expansion in the future?

sources.title: Possible Theoretical limits on holographic quintessence from weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Solve the density initial-value problem, integrate the scalar excursion, scan the parameters, trace the unit-excursion contour, and fit the resulting boundary points. Finite upper bounds require the contour to intersect the selected parameter slice.

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Absorb the phenomenological interaction into an effective vacuum pressure, reconstruct a canonical background scalar from that effective stress tensor, and integrate its redshift derivative. Changing the decay law requires solving the interaction and background again.

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Translate the component's density and equation of state into its canonical field speed, change the integration variable to redshift, and integrate. Apply the field-range conjecture to that excursion rather than directly to w.

sources.title: Dark Energy: A Brief Review

evidence.text: Observational methods combine distance and growth probes, supernova χ² fitting with nuisance-H₀ marginalization, and parameter-penalized model comparison: BIC = −2 ln Lmax + k ln N and AIC = −2 ln Lmax + 2k. The χ² identification assumes Gaussian likelihoods.

sources.title: The Effective Field Theory of Dark Energy

evidence.text: Analyze quadratic kinetic actions in Newtonian gauge using Fourier-space kinetic determinants, constraints and local field redefinitions. Obtain Newtonian responses by neglecting time derivatives and adding pressureless matter sources.

sources.title: Cosmological Evolution With Interaction Between Dark Energy And Dark Matter

evidence.text: Use autonomous dynamical systems, critical points, linear perturbations and Jacobian eigenvalues to classify stationary ratios and their stability. Effective interaction pressure Π, defined through Q=−3HΠ, provides another parametrization.

sources.title: Perspectives on the Dark Sector

evidence.text: What limitations does point-particle EFT face in explaining dark energy and primordial structure, and what prospects do a heterotic unified dark sector and high-temperature matrix-model emergent cosmology offer?

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: How do constant dark-energy equation of state and present matter abundance jointly determine the expansion history and scalar density fraction?

sources.title: Model-Independent Perspectives on Coupled Dark Energy and the Swampland

evidence.text: The assumed cosmology allows dark matter to exchange energy with dark energy while baryons remain separately conserved. A canonical scalar supplies a physical realization; a general fluid supplies a broader background description without a nonphantom restriction.

sources.title: Swampland Conjectures and Late-Time Cosmology

evidence.text: How much can a canonical dark-energy scalar evolve while preserving the observed late-time expansion and linear perturbations?

sources.title: Interplay between Swampland and Bayesian Machine Learning in constraining cosmological models

evidence.text: The background setting asks whether an accelerating expansion can be represented by a homogeneous canonical scalar together with separately conserved pressureless dark matter in general relativity.

sources.title: A stringy perspective on the coincidence problem

evidence.text: Why observe comparable matter and dark-energy densities if acceleration has an indefinitely long future? The paper investigates whether limiting that future reduces the temporal coincidence.

sources.title: Early dark sector, the Hubble tension, and the swampland

evidence.text: How does a scalar-dependent particle mass couple an early-dark-energy field to cold dark matter? The source models the matter as nonrelativistic Dirac fermions whose total number density sources the scalar.

sources.title: Testing the Swampland: $H_0$ tension

evidence.text: The model follows a homogeneous canonical dark-energy scalar evolving with pressureless matter. It supplies the background expansion histories whose present normalization is inferred from low-redshift Hubble-parameter measurements.

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: Does an observationally simple decoupling of the visible and dark-energy sectors satisfy a conjecture imposed everywhere in scalar field space?

sources.title: Hubble sinks in the low-redshift swampland

evidence.text: How does a dark-matter interaction modify the expansion driven by a canonical scalar? Normalizing the interaction to unity today permits an effective phantom history without introducing a phantom scalar kinetic term.

sources.title: The Coincidence Problem and the Swampland Conjectures in the Ijjas-Steinhardt Cyclic Model of the Universe

evidence.text: Can a nonsingular universe with repeatedly similar radiation, matter and scalar-driven expansion phases make the current matter–dark-energy coincidence typical in cosmic time?

sources.title: Hubble sinks in the low-redshift swampland

evidence.text: Can dark-matter coupling produce apparent phantom dark energy while the scalar remains canonical? The adopted present normalization fixes a nonphantom effective value today, while evolution at positive redshift can change that behavior.

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Can the effects assigned to Dark Energy arise from averaging ordinary inhomogeneous matter and geometry in Einstein gravity? The question includes whether an FLRW prior changes the interpretation of observations taken on different scales and at different epochs.

sources.title: Model-Independent Perspectives on Coupled Dark Energy and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which properties of an interacting dark sector can be inferred from the Universe's background expansion? The paper asks how an assumed dark-energy equation of state or coupling history enables reconstruction of the other function and of canonical scalar-potential diagnostics.

sources.title: $H_0$ tension, swampland conjectures, and the epoch of fading dark matter

evidence.text: Can scalar-dependent dark-matter mass affect recent expansion without altering the early universe appreciably? The model delays mass variation until a scalar threshold, then allows dark matter to lose rest-mass energy as the scalar rolls.

sources.title: Scalar dark energy models mimicking $\Lambda$CDM with arbitrary future evolution

evidence.text: Can scalar or fluid dark energy reproduce the observed ΛCDM-like expansion through the present while allowing substantially different future evolution, including delayed disruption of bound structures and finite-time singularities?

sources.title: Machine Learning and cosmographic reconstructions of quintessence and the Swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can cosmological observations reconstruct a canonical dark-energy scalar and distinguish changes in expansion from changes in growth and lensing without selecting a particular scalar potential?

sources.title: AdS - de Sitter transition in interacting dark energy models

evidence.text: Can a general linear dark-sector interaction dynamically change dark-energy density from negative to positive while preserving nonnegative dark-matter density and remaining compatible with supernova, BAO and CMB observations?

sources.title: Evolution of dark energy reconstructed from the latest observations

evidence.text: Do the observational datasets used in this 2018 analysis favor evolution of effective dark energy density when negative densities are permitted, and how does that preference depend on the reconstruction prior?

sources.title: Quantum Fine-Tuning in Stringy Quintessence Models

evidence.text: The models must reproduce a very small positive energy density and nearly vacuum-like equation of state. Their scalar must remain light on the present Hubble scale, making even small radiative masses and long-range matter couplings consequential.

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Does an inhomogeneous universe evolve on average like an FLRW solution, and can structure-induced backreaction explain apparent Dark Energy within classical general relativity? This status report reviews the mechanism and strategies for establishing its quantitative and observational relevance.

sources.title: Isocurvature Perturbations of Dark Energy and Dark Matter from the Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: What happens if dark-matter rest masses depend exponentially on the scalar driving present acceleration?

sources.title: The Coincidence Problem and the Swampland Conjectures in the Ijjas-Steinhardt Cyclic Model of the Universe

evidence.text: Can the observed matter–dark-energy coincidence infer the duration of the current cycle when the cyclic model does not predict that duration?

sources.title: String-Inspired Running Vacuum—The “Vacuumon”—And the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: The cosmological evolution is described through interacting vacuum and matter components, a canonical scalar representation, and an axion–condensate system. Comparing these descriptions requires separate field and energy-component dictionaries.

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: Could a drainon also account for dark matter while a cosmological constant explains current acceleration?

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Can two exponential terms provide both an early scaling era and a later dark-energy era compatible with observations? The source considers scaling-freezing and nonscaling histories.

sources.title: Swampland criteria in the slotheon field dark energy

evidence.text: Which externally reconstructed equation-of-state envelopes are used to assess scalar dark-energy histories?

sources.title: Reconstructing Quintessence

evidence.text: Determine which properties of a canonical dark-energy scalar can be inferred from cosmological observations without committing to a potential formula. The targets include its equation of state, traversed potential, field excursion and dynamical trajectories.

sources.title: Early dark sector, the Hubble tension, and the swampland

evidence.text: Can cosmological bounds on a scalar-dependent dark-matter mass challenge an SDC-motivated early-dark-energy model when the fraction of coupled matter is not fixed by the conjecture?

sources.title: The Coincidence Problem and the Swampland Conjectures in the Ijjas-Steinhardt Cyclic Model of the Universe

evidence.text: Matter dilutes as a^-3, whereas dark energy with w near -1 dilutes much more slowly. The coincidence question asks why the current densities are comparable. This paper evaluates whether comparable densities occupy a substantial fraction of cosmic time.

sources.title: Emergent dark energy from unparticles

evidence.text: Can the collective thermal behavior of a sector slightly displaced from a conformal fixed point generate late-time dark energy through a limiting temperature, while behaving like radiation early enough to satisfy cosmological constraints?

sources.title: New Scalar Field Quartessence

evidence.text: Can one scalar dark component simultaneously support spatially clustered, particle-like dark matter and a nearly homogeneous dark-energy background at late times, rather than simply replacing an early matter phase with a late dark-energy phase?

sources.title: Swampland criteria in the slotheon field dark energy

evidence.text: How do initially frozen scalar fields evolve into the observed late-time dark-energy component while maintaining approximately the observed present matter fraction?

destination.title: Antibrane uplift: stabilization, consistency and effective descriptions
destination.question: Under which source-specific assumptions can antibrane uplift coexist with moduli stabilization, compact embedding and a reliable effective description?
destination.summary: No original prose scope was supplied, so the original proposal is assessed through its numerical membership. Its main concentration is coherent as a broad research family, not as one equivalent question. Local uplift matching, dynamical conifold response, global construction, decay channels, towers and phenomenology remain separate targets. The K3 degeneration comparison is retained as an alternate direction.

systems: KKLT/KKLMMT and LVS constructions where explicitly identified
Antibranes and specified positive-tension uplift sources in compactification throats
Four-dimensional EFTs and conditional higher-dimensional descriptions

regimes: Source-specific strong, weak and unequal-throat warping
Leading-order and explicitly corrected effective descriptions
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work as well as proposed quantum-gravity tests

conventions: Integrated ten-dimensional consistency constraints are distinct from D3-charge budgets
AdS precursor construction, uplift and post-uplift stability are separate stages

An alternate navigation home for the fixed-volume K3 comparison
excludes: Treating numerical proximity as scientific equivalence

A universal no-go theorem or certification of controlled string de Sitter vacua

sources.title: Constraints on Dbar Uplifts

evidence.text: Under what conditions do anti-D3 uplifts in KKLT/KKLMMT and LVS admit a valid effective description of inflation and reheating, and when do one-loop corrections preserve classical soft-mass predictions?

sources.title: Uplifting Runaways

evidence.text: Does an anti-D3 uplift preserve the finite conifold deformation when that field remains dynamical? The question includes a single antibrane and motivates examining whether analogous positive energy from a horizon can also change the deformation.

sources.title: Gaugino condensation and small uplifts in KKLT

evidence.text: Can uplifted KKLT vacua satisfy the ten-dimensional integrated tadpole constraint, and can a throat producing a sufficiently small uplift fit inside a controlled compactification?

sources.title: On de Sitter String Vacua from Anti-D3-Branes in the Large Volume Scenario

evidence.text: Can a concrete type IIB Calabi–Yau orientifold support anti-D3 uplift to an LVS de Sitter minimum while stabilising the throat modulus, controlling approximations, avoiding runaways and satisfying D3-tadpole cancellation?

sources.title: LVS de Sitter vacua are probably in the swampland

evidence.text: This EFT tests moduli stabilization and anti-D3 uplift in a strongly warped conifold glued into a two-Kähler-modulus Calabi–Yau orientifold. It retains the conifold deformation instead of freezing the entire complex-structure sector.

sources.title: Mass Hierarchies and Quantum Gravity Constraints in DKMM-refined KKLT

evidence.text: Does generating exponentially small W0 through the conifold extension of DKMM permit controlled KKLT stabilization and anti-D3 uplift, once throat geometry, bulk/throat mass hierarchies, species scales and tadpole cancellation are considered together?

sources.title: Curvature corrections to KPV: do we need deep throats?

evidence.text: How do order-α′² curvature corrections change KPV metastability and the throat size needed for anti-brane uplifts? Could curvature-induced tension reduction replace hierarchical warping?

sources.title: Constraints on Dbar Uplifts

evidence.text: An interpolating ten-dimensional metric is used to extract string scales from the world-sheet action and KK scales from internal harmonic expansions, distinguishing unwarped bulk modes from modes supported in a strongly warped throat.

sources.title: Uplifting Runaways

evidence.text: Evaluate tension and RR-charge contributions, substitute the warped background, and minimize radial placement. Since I(T) decreases, the anti-D3 energy is minimized at the tip.

sources.title: Gaugino condensation and small uplifts in KKLT

evidence.text: Integrate the ten-dimensional equation for Φ− over the compact space, then relate the seven-brane stress trace to variations of a general internal-metric functional along the overall volume mode. Separately combine throat-size, warping and KKLT stabilization scalings.

sources.title: On de Sitter String Vacua from Anti-D3-Branes in the Large Volume Scenario

evidence.text: Expand at large volume and large aτ_s, with uplift balance ζ^{4/3}∼W₀²/V^{5/3}. Extremise the resulting potential, separate the phase directions, and analyse stability through the Kähler-metric-weighted Hessian.

sources.title: LVS de Sitter vacua are probably in the swampland

evidence.text: Specialize general vev and mass expressions to the stated AdS setup, omit prescribed terms and remove uplift. Inspect surviving corrections rather than assuming that removing uplift restores control.

sources.title: Mass Hierarchies and Quantum Gravity Constraints in DKMM-refined KKLT

evidence.text: Solve the radial warped Laplace eigenproblem with Neumann conditions at both throat ends and the stated normalization ∫|χn|²dy=1. An assumed one-dimensional KK tower is also used for one-loop matching to the tree-level field-space metric.

sources.title: On K3-fibred LARGE Volume Scenario with de Sitter vacua from anti-D3-branes

evidence.text: Can a K3-fibred LVS compactification admit an explicit anti-D3 uplift with suitable O3-planes, sufficient negative D3 charge, and stabilization of the additional Kähler directions under the stated effective-field-theory assumptions?

sources.title: Bounds on tower mass scales in the presence of throats of different warping

evidence.text: When an uplift-producing throat is less strongly warped than another throat, how do de Sitter unitarity and the four-dimensional supergravity hierarchy constrain the uplift-related tower scale in terms of the lower tower scale?

sources.title: The LVS parametric tadpole constraint

evidence.text: How much negative D3 tadpole is required for LVS de Sitter constructions with anti-D3 throat uplift when warping and higher F-term corrections must meet a prescribed quality of parametric control?

sources.title: On uplifts by warped anti‐D3‐branes

evidence.text: Does the simplest single-modulus KKLT construction admit a controlled warped anti-D3 uplift to de Sitter, assuming gaugino condensation has a ten-dimensional description, and can four-dimensional supergravity parametrizations encode the authors’ proposed obstruction?

sources.title: Effective Theory of Warped Compactifications and the Implications for KKLT

evidence.text: How do higher-dimensional gravitational constraints modify the off-shell potential of the Klebanov–Strassler conifold deformation parameter, and does the corrected response remove the previously proposed antibrane-induced runaway relevant to KKLT uplift?

sources.title: Candidate de Sitter vacua

evidence.text: Can explicit Calabi–Yau orientifolds and quantized fluxes simultaneously realize moduli stabilization, a suitably warped Klebanov–Strassler throat and anti-D3 uplift to metastable de Sitter space in a specified leading-order EFT?

sources.title: α′ corrections to KPV: an uplifting story

evidence.text: How do known curvature, gauge-field, and flux corrections modify KPV metastability, and can they supply a small positive uplift without a deep warped throat? What control and D3-tadpole requirements follow?

sources.title: Control issues of KKLT

evidence.text: Does KKLT admit quantitatively controlled ten-dimensional supergravity backgrounds once nonperturbative Kähler stabilization and a warped anti-D3 uplift are required, and does obtaining the necessary large tadpole introduce additional control problems?

sources.title: A 10d view on the KKLT AdS vacuum and uplifting

evidence.text: Can a local semiclassical ten-dimensional treatment of D7 gaugino condensation reproduce the KKLT AdS vacuum and establish whether anti-D3 sources permit a metastable dS uplift?

sources.title: Understanding KKLT from a 10d perspective

evidence.text: Do integrated trace-reversed ten-dimensional Einstein equations obstruct KKLT de Sitter uplift once D7 gaugino condensation, its volume dependence, and a strongly warped positive-tension uplift source are treated consistently?

sources.title: Open string moduli in KKLT compactifications

evidence.text: How strongly does compactification lift the anti-D3 position moduli at the tip of a KKLT throat, and can orientifold planes raise their masses?

sources.title: Uplift and towers of states in warped throat

evidence.text: How does antibrane uplift correlate with towers of states across strong and weak warping, and what constraints follow for a reliable EFT and its superpotential?

sources.title: Bare-bones de Sitter vacua

evidence.text: Can anti-D3 branes supply both the uplift and the small superpotential needed for Kähler-modulus stabilization, allowing de Sitter minima without an independently introduced supersymmetry-breaking flux superpotential?

sources.title: Supersymmetry Breaking Warped Throats and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can compactification stop a runaway while preserving a tunable redshift hierarchy? Can further quantum-gravity criteria constrain metastable uplift throats?

sources.title: Moduli Stabilisation with Nilpotent Goldstino: Vacuum Structure and SUSY Breaking

evidence.text: How does a nilpotent-superfield description of warped anti-D3 uplift affect KKLT/LVS vacua, visible-sector soft terms and the stability of D3-branes at singularities?

sources.title: KKLT and the Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can nonperturbatively stabilized, strongly warped KKLT vacua satisfy proposed quantum-gravity constraints, and does their effective theory remain reliable after including throat states?

sources.title: Toward de Sitter space from ten dimensions

evidence.text: Is single-condensate KKLT volume stabilization sufficiently rigid for anti-D3 uplift to de Sitter, and can racetrack stabilization evade the proposed obstruction in a ten-dimensional description?

sources.title: Dynamics of warped flux compactifications with backreacting antibranes

evidence.text: Does dimensional reduction with anti-D3 backreaction reproduce the leading probe uplift coefficient and volume scaling relevant to KKLT/KKLMMT, and what near-brane boundary condition is required for agreement?

sources.title: Brief overview of Candidate de Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: Can explicit type-IIB Calabi–Yau orientifolds simultaneously realise small-energy supersymmetric AdS precursors, appropriately redshifted Klebanov–Strassler throats, and anti-D3 uplift to metastable de Sitter minima? This proceedings review summarises the construction reported in its underlying study.
